name: IT Ops
title: IT Ops: AI on-call engineer for IT incidents | Singularity
description: IT Ops is an AI on-call engineer. It groups alerts into one incident, finds the cause, applies the fix with your approval and records every step.
h1: IT failures resolved faster, safely and on the record.
lede: IT Ops is an AI on-call engineer. It groups scattered alerts into one incident, finds the cause with evidence, proposes a fix, applies it with your approval and records every step.

items.p: Finding the cause often takes longer than fixing it. At 3 a.m. the on-call engineer chases it across several screens.
The fix lives in the heads of a few experienced staff. What happens when they are on leave?
Who did what, and why? Often it is recorded nowhere, so management and auditors get no clear answer.

steps.title: Four steps. The same routine every time.

items.p: Groups scattered alerts from your monitoring tools into one incident, so it is clear which service is hit and who owns it.
Finds the cause and shows the evidence. It also says plainly when it is not sure.
Proposes a fix from a list you approved and, when needed, sends it to the owner for approval.
Applies the fix and measures the result. If it does not work, it undoes the change and alerts a person.
Your team starts from a recommendation backed by evidence instead of hunting for the cause.
One decision card at night instead of many screens. It arrives on the web, in Microsoft Teams or in Slack.
Every fix that worked is remembered, so new hires follow the same playbook.
Who did what, and why, is always on record, and later changes are detected. Management gets a PDF report.
IT Ops reads the tools you already run. Your team keeps working in the screens it knows.
It starts by only watching. You decide when it may recommend, fix in test and fix in production.

fit.title: Not another tool. A bridge between yours.

control.title: As risk grows, a person steps in

items.p: IT Ops cannot write its own commands. It picks from a list of fixes you approved, on systems you listed.
Checks run on their own. High-impact fixes always need a person. One button halts every automated action on your systems.
IT Ops is installed in your environment. Passwords, names and addresses are masked in any text sent to the AI.

faq.a: IT Ops is an AI on-call engineer from Singularity. It groups alerts from your monitoring tools into one incident, finds the cause with evidence, proposes a fix, applies it with your approval, checks the result and records every step.

IT Ops is for companies whose IT teams are on call for outages. IT managers get a less exhausted team, security and compliance teams get every step logged, and executives get shorter outages with AI kept under control.

faq.q: How is IT Ops different from a monitoring tool?
faq.a: A monitoring tool tells you something is wrong. IT Ops reads the alerts from the tools you already have, finds the cause, proposes a fix, applies it with approval and keeps the record. Your existing tools stay in place.

faq.q: Can IT Ops run on-premises or air-gapped?
faq.a: Yes. IT Ops is installed in your own environment and works in air-gapped networks, which have no internet connection. You choose the AI provider, and it can run on the Singularity Foundation Models on your own hardware.

faq.q: How do people stay in control of IT Ops?
faq.a: IT Ops cannot write its own commands. It picks fixes from a list you approved, on systems you listed. High-impact fixes always wait for a person’s approval, nobody can approve their own request, and one button stops every automated action.

cta.h: See IT Ops on your own incidents
cta.p: We handle the setup. IT Ops starts by only watching and recommending, and you decide when it may act.
